# libsodium / crypto_sign_fuzzer

OSS-Fuzz's fuzz target `crypto_sign_fuzzer` ([source](source/crypto_sign_fuzzer.cc), unmodified) over libsodium (jedisct1/libsodium at 2c61b499).

Checks 3 properties (listed below); the first, a self-validation: An Ed25519 detached signature just made over the input message with an input-seeded key must verify under the matching public key.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libsodium at commit 2c61b499.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- An Ed25519 detached signature just made over the input message with an input-seeded key must verify under the matching public key ([lines 47-52](source/crypto_sign_fuzzer.cc#L47-L52)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.
- Multi-part (Ed25519ph) signature built with init/update(two halves)/final_create must verify with a fresh init/update(same halves)/final_verify ([lines 54-68](source/crypto_sign_fuzzer.cc#L54-L68)): assert(); confirmed in the binary.

A failed check marked as ending the process contradicts every halts statement below, so a proof of one implies them on every input it covers.

Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libsodium` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
